title: Kremlin Says Modi and Xi Offered Putin Help to End Ukraine War
excerpt: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the leaders of India and China offered their 'good offices' to help find a settlement during bilateral meetings with Vladimir Putin in New Delhi ahead of the BRICS summit.
body:
• Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping offered their "good offices" to help find a settlement to the Ukraine war during bilateral meetings with Vladimir Putin.
  • Peskov said Putin welcomed the offers and briefed both leaders in detail on the situation surrounding the conflict.
  • The offers came during Modi-Putin talks in New Delhi on Friday — their second meeting this year — on the eve of the BRICS leaders' summit in the Indian capital, which Xi is attending.
  • The diplomacy unfolds as U.S. peace efforts face hurdles and fighting between Russia and Ukraine has escalated in recent weeks.

Russian President Vladimir Putin has received offers from the leaders of India and China to help broker an end to the war in Ukraine, the Kremlin said, placing two of Moscow's most important partners in a potential mediating role.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping made the offers during bilateral meetings with Putin, taking what he described as a keen interest in a settlement. Putin welcomed their readiness to help and briefed both leaders in detail on the situation surrounding the conflict, Peskov added.

Modi met Putin in New Delhi on Friday for talks expected to focus on trade, energy and defence — the second meeting between the two leaders this year, after they spoke on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, on August 31. The talks were held on the eve of the annual BRICS leaders' summit in the Indian capital, which Xi is attending alongside leaders including Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.

Context & Background

At the Bishkek meeting, Modi told Putin the war needed to end for humanity's sake and pledged that New Delhi would support every peace effort to stop the fighting, according to a Kremlin transcript of their exchange. Putin visited India in December 2025 for the annual India-Russia summit, where the two countries agreed to expand their trade and defence relationship.

"Every day that the war continues, humanity is, in effect, set back a step, whilst every step towards peace gives all of humanity real hope for peace."

— Narendra Modi, Prime Minister of India, to Vladimir Putin in Bishkek

The new diplomatic opening comes as persistent efforts by U.S. President Donald Trump to broker a peace deal between Moscow and Kyiv continue to face hurdles. U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner recently traveled to Moscow and Kyiv in an effort to restart negotiations — but despite the renewed diplomatic push, fighting between Russia and Ukraine continued this week amid an escalation in recent weeks.

Impact & Analysis

"During their bilateral meetings, Modi and Xi took a keen interest in the Ukraine settlement and actively offered their good offices to help find a solution."

— Dmitry Peskov, Kremlin spokesman, quoted by Sputnik

The weight of the offers lies in who is making them. India and China are the biggest buyers of Russian oil — together accounting for about 90% of Russia's oil exports — and Russia's share of Indian crude imports reached a record 51% in July, according to Reuters, as disruptions to Middle Eastern supplies deepened Indian refiners' reliance on Russian barrels. That economic leverage gives both leaders a channel to Moscow that Western governments do not have.

In New Delhi, Modi and Putin also advanced the bilateral agenda: closer trade ties, including implementation of the Programme for Economic Cooperation 2030, and cooperation in civil nuclear energy, fertilisers, defence, critical minerals, manufacturing, railways and steel, according to an Indian source cited by Reuters. Modi later wrote on X that he was delighted to meet Putin in Delhi, less than two weeks after their Bishkek meeting.

India's official line, reiterated after Friday's talks, is that the Ukraine conflict can be resolved only through dialogue and diplomacy — and that New Delhi stands ready to contribute to peace efforts and support initiatives aimed at resolving conflicts through dialogue.

What's Next

Attention now turns to the BRICS summit in New Delhi, where Ukraine is likely to feature in leaders' discussions alongside trade and development. Whether the offers from Modi and Xi evolve into a formal mediation track remains to be seen; for now, the Kremlin has welcomed the gesture, Putin has briefed both leaders, and the fighting shows no sign of abating.
